additions.reason: Hitbodedut (secluded personal prayer/conversation with God) is the opening and dominant concept of the Torah. It is presented as the practice that initiates the reciprocal dynamic. It is bechina-identical to 'פְּרִישׁוּת שִׂיחָה וְצַעַר' (articulating speech and pain), since the Torah defines hitbodedut as precisely that act. It corresponds to the 'אֶת ה' הֶאֱמַרְתָּ' side of the central bechina verse.
additions.source_quote: כְּשֶׁאָדָם מִתְבּוֹדֵד וּמְפָרֵשׁ שִׂיחָתוֹ וְצַעֲרוֹ לִפְנֵי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ

additions.reason: Articulating one's speech and pain before God is bechina-identical to hitbodedut (they are defined as the same act) and is simultaneously bechina-parallel to the Shekhinah's corresponding act ('מְפָרֶשֶׁת לְפָנָיו שִׂיחָתָהּ וְצַעֲרָהּ'). This is the explicit bechina structure of the teaching: the human's speech = the Shekhinah's speech, as two aspects of mutual declaration ('אֶת ה' הֶאֱמַרְתָּ וַה' הֶאֱמִירְךָ').
additions.source_quote: וּמְפָרֵשׁ שִׂיחָתוֹ וְצַעֲרוֹ לִפְנֵי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ

additions.reason: Confession (viduy) and regret (charata) are paired together by the Rebbe as integral parts of the hitbodedut act. They are not listed as cause-and-effect ('through confessing you achieve X') but as simultaneous components of the same practice. The person articulates speech, confesses, and regrets — all as one act of מִתְבּוֹדֵד. These are aspects of the same 'declaring God' (אֶת ה' הֶאֱמַרְתָּ) that the hitbodedut embodies.
additions.source_quote: וּמִתְוַדֶּה וּמִתְחָרֵט עַל גֹּדֶל הַפְּגָמִים שֶׁעָשָׂה

additions.reason: The Shekhinah (Divine Presence) is the primary entity on the divine-response side of the central bechina. She is presented as the being who 'correspondingly' (כְּנֶגְדּוֹ) articulates her speech and pain and comforts the person — she is the active subject of the 'וַה' הֶאֱמִירְךָ' (the Lord declared you) side of the bechina verse. The Shekhinah IS this responsive-divine-presence-who-mirrors-the-human, making her the dominant node of the Shekhinah-response dimension of the package.
additions.source_quote: אֲזַי גַּם הַשְּׁכִינָה כְּנֶגְדּוֹ מְפָרֶשֶׁת לְפָנָיו שִׂיחָתָהּ וְצַעֲרָהּ וּמְנַחֶמֶת אוֹתוֹ

additions.reason: The Shekhinah's articulation of her speech and pain is structurally parallel (bechina) to the human's articulation of his speech and pain. This is the explicit bechina the Rebbe establishes: just as the human speaks his pain (פְּרִישׁוּת שִׂיחָה וְצַעַר), the Shekhinah correspondingly speaks her pain. The two together ARE the verse 'אֶת ה' הֶאֱמַרְתָּ וַה' הֶאֱמִירְךָ' — mutual speech/declaration. Polarity is good: the Shekhinah's pain and speech are part of the holy domain.

Comfort/consolation (נִחוּם) is what the Shekhinah provides to the person after articulating her shared pain with him. It is one of the three expressions of the Shekhinah's 'וַה' הֶאֱמִירְךָ' response (speech, pain, and comforting). This is the redemptive dimension of the bechina: the Shekhinah's comforting is the human's being comforted, since they share the same reality.

The flaw in the soul (פְּגָם בַּנְּשָׁמָה) is explicitly stated as bechina-identical to a flaw in the Shekhinah: 'כָּל פְּגָם וּפְגָם שֶׁפָּגַם בְּנִשְׁמָתוֹ, פָּגַם אֶצְלָהּ גַּם כֵּן'. The two flaws are two expressions of the same damage. This is a core bechina pair in the Torah. Polarity is 'good' (i.e., it belongs to the good/holy package) because the flaw in the soul is the motivating awareness that leads to hitbodedut and teshuvah — it is the background reality that the good practice addresses. It is not an evil concept in itself here; it is the problem that the good teaching solves.
additions.source_quote: כִּי כָּל פְּגָם וּפְגָם שֶׁפָּגַם בְּנִשְׁמָתוֹ, פָּגַם אֶצְלָהּ גַּם כֵּן כִּבְיָכוֹל

additions.reason: This verse (Deuteronomy 26:17) is the proof-text and the named bechina in the Torah. The Rebbe explicitly says 'וְזֶה בְּחִינַת' (and this is the bechina of) this verse. The verse IS the bechina — it is the conceptual key that names and captures the mutual-declaration reality that the entire Torah describes. It belongs in the package as the named bechina node that all other nodes resolve into.
additions.source_quote: וְזֶה בְּחִינַת (דברים כו): אֶת ה' הֶאֱמַרְתָּ וַה' הֶאֱמִירְךָ וְכוּ'

additions.reason: The Shekhinah comforts the person by telling him she will seek 'remedies/schemes to repair all the flaws' (תַּחְבּוּלוֹת לְתַקֵּן כָּל הַפְּגָמִים). This is the constructive/restorative dimension of the Shekhinah's response — the forward-looking, repair-oriented face of her 'comforting'. It is bechina-related to נִחוּם (it IS the content of the comforting: the assurance of repair) and is one of the expressions of the Shekhinah's 'וַה' הֶאֱמִירְךָ' reality.
additions.source_quote: וְהִיא מְנַחֶמֶת אוֹתוֹ שֶׁתְּבַקֵּשׁ תַּחְבּוּלוֹת לְתַקֵּן כָּל הַפְּגָמִים

There are no orphaned dataset nodes (the dataset is empty for this Torah).

bechina_structure_summary.central_bechina: The mutual-speech/declaration dynamic between the human (hitbodedut, articulating speech and pain) and the Shekhinah (articulating her speech and pain, comforting) IS (בְּחִינַת) the verse 'אֶת ה' הֶאֱמַרְתָּ וַה' הֶאֱמִירְךָ' (Deuteronomy 26:17).
bechina_structure_summary.secondary_bechina: Every flaw in the human's soul IS simultaneously a flaw in the Shekhinah — stated as explicit structural equivalence: 'כָּל פְּגָם וּפְגָם שֶׁפָּגַם בְּנִשְׁמָתוֹ, פָּגַם אֶצְלָהּ גַּם כֵּן'.
bechina_structure_summary.eitza_connections_present: The teaching also contains eitza elements: hitbodedut → Shekhinah's response (the human's action triggers/corresponds to the Shekhinah's response). But the relationship between the human's speech and the Shekhinah's speech is BECHINA (they are mirror expressions of the same reality), not eitza (the human's speech does not 'produce' the Shekhinah's speech as a separate causal event — they are simultaneous co-expressions of the same mutual-declaration dynamic).
